source_text: Si quis homicidium conscientia formidante commiserit, reus est, quia timuit; si autem aliquod facinus exsultante perpetrarit audacia, velut credens se ex fide facere quod male facit, evasit culpam
pass_a_gloss: If who homicidium conscientia formidante commiserit, guilty is, because timuit; if however aliquod facinus exsultante perpetrarit audacia, as-if credens himself from fide to-make that/which badly makes, evasit fault.
pass_b_english: If someone commits murder while their conscience is afraid, they are guilty because they were afraid. But if they commit some crime with triumphant boldness, as though believing that they do their evil deed from faith, they escape guilt.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded. This row is Augustine's report; Pass A glosses only the Julian words recoverable here.
